note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.” Zephaniah names who is on that list: “it shall come to pass in the day of the Lord’s sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.” Strange apparel goes against what the Bible says, like women in pants.

That day is the evil time, and “A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked”, for neither their silver nor their gold is going to save them in it. The righteous “shall not be ashamed in the evil time: and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.” That is why we have food pantries in our cities: when the days of famine come, the Most High will make sure we are satisfied. All you have to do is get in touch with your leadership in your state, and there is no shame in it.

precepts.text: Neither their silver nor their gold shall deliver them in the day of the Most High's wrath, for the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
Zephaniah says the same of the day of the Lord: “Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord’s wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy”. He will “make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.” Those who boast in the multitude of their riches will find their silver and gold cannot ransom them when the wrath comes.

Riches profit not in the day of wrath, and they cannot redeem a brother from the grave. Trust in uncertain riches fails at both ends; the living God is the only sure trust.

precepts.why: The way you dress stipulates what you believe: you know a Roman Catholic priest, a Buddhist, a Muslim by their clothes. “I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.” God says he will destroy those in strange apparel. He gave us a dress code: fringes, and a border of blue upon all your garments.
“The word of the Lord which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi”. Zephaniah is a prophet; we read his book. And he was the son of Cushi: his father was called black.

Zephaniah 1:7 said the Lord hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests; this is what we’re looking for. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Who’s Idumea, brothers? Edom, the so-called white man.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams: for the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea.” A sacrifice. Put Bozrah up on the screen: Bozrah is right there in the land of Israel.

What is he calling the nations in verse six? The blood of lambs and of goats, the fat of the kidneys of rams: he’s talking about the nations. A sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea: these are all symbolizing the people of Idumea. “And the unicorns shall come down with them”: the unicorns, the rhinoceros, is another name for the nations. “And the bullocks with the bulls”: now he calls them bullocks. “And their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness.” Why? “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” He’s going to get vengeance on all the nations.

So in Isaiah 34 God calls the nations other names: he calls them Idumea, and then gives them animal names for a sacrifice. That is the sacrifice the Lord has prepared in the day of the Lord in Zephaniah 1:7.

Start at verse one: “Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear, and all that is therein”. Underline it, put it in your notes: ye nations. The chapter is spoken to the nations, so when verse six speaks of lambs and goats and rams, it is the nations that are the sacrifice.

Who are the masters whose houses are filled with violence? “And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” Who were the masters, brothers? The Israelites.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence”. See that: the kingdom of heaven suffers violence. He’s talking about the Israelites. Nobody was jumping up into the skies and fighting with the Father; he ain’t talking about that. The kingdom of heaven, the Israelites, suffereth violence.

“And the violent take it by force.” Who took the land of Israel, brothers? Rome, Amalek, the white man. So those that leap on our threshold and fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit in Zephaniah 1:9 are the white man.

“Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.” Now go back to Zephaniah 1:13: “they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof.” It is the same curse. You might think it ended there, in the past, but no.

This is prophetic for every captivity, including this one. “O my people, hear my word: make you ready to thy battle, and in those evils be even as pilgrims upon the earth.” Brothers and sisters, be as pilgrims on the earth; but the main part is, make you ready for the battle.

“He that selleth, let him be as he that fleeth away: and he that buyeth, as one that will lose: He that occupieth merchandise, as he that hath no profit by it: and he that buildeth, as he that shall not dwell therein”: the same as they shall build houses but not inhabit them.

Jump over to get to the point. “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord. They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” That’s going to come upon us soon.

“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” Some of us will be cast out of our houses. “Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

How? We showed you T-Mobile and all of the carriers implementing fines for the type of speech you carry. That is how we’re going to begin to lose what we have. Their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: just as it happened in the past, during the time of Babylon and in every captivity, even today it is going to happen.

A day of the trumpet: a trumpet represented a warning that danger is coming. “Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet”: lift up your voice like a trumpet. That’s to you teachers out there. “And shew my people their transgression”: show the Israelites their transgressions, “and the house of Jacob their sins.”

“I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the Lord.” The land is the land of Israel. That means everything is going to be destroyed in the land of Israel, and that has not happened yet.

“I will consume man and beast”; “and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the Lord.” Destruction came during the time of Babylon, but man was not consumed off the land. During the time of Persia and Media, man was not consumed from off the land. Remember, during the time of Babylon they kept the poor in the land: the poorest of the people stayed in the land. The same through the Greeks and the Romans. That is letting you know the scriptures are doubled to that which is written, as we read earlier.

“I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem”. You might say, wait a minute, Judah’s not in the land today. Who told you our people are not in Jerusalem today? We were in Jerusalem; our people are there. There are many articles on it. We’re not there ruling, but we are there.

Look at this one from The Times of Israel: ‘Who are the Black Hebrews, the group linked to Jersey City shooter.’ They linked the Jersey City shooting all the way to our people in the land of Israel, people who haven’t been to Jersey since the 1960s. And the officers said, that’s what we thought too, but our superiors wanted it. Everything in my house is videotaped, so in case the ADL wants to say I’m a liar, I will show the video.

And when our people are put in the IDF, if they don’t say what they want them to say, they get kicked out of the land; that’s the stipulation.

“And I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests”. What is this word Chemarims? Look it up: ‘those who go about in black’, applied to the priests of the worship of false gods. In neo-Hebrew it designates a Catholic priest or monk. It is associated with the verb kamar, to be black, and the meaning priest comes from the circumstance that the priests wore black garments. Not only do the Catholic priests wear black: who else wears black? These so-called Jewish people and the Catholic priests. They all got black on. It’s talking about them.

Read further in that dictionary: the old Semitic idols were without exception worshipped by intemperate sexual excesses; the hot, exciting man was the priest. Look at the video of these guys praying: they make sexual thrusts with their hips. Hot, exciting men, humping sensations. You can’t make this stuff up. That’s the Chemarims. If not them, then who? Who’s in the land of Israel wearing all black that’s hot and exciting when they pray? That’s them humping the wall. Y’all get mad at me online if you want, but it’s the truth.

“And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the Lord, and that swear by Malcham”. Look Malcham up: it was a reference to the god of pleasure. And look at them when they’re praying: one pump, two pumps, three pumps, and they be grinding. Who prays like that? He’s the god of pleasure. You’re nasty.

“And them that are turned back from the Lord; and those that have not sought the Lord, nor enquired for him.” Now this is our people; verse six is going into our people. How have they turned back from the Lord? They are not following what the Bible says. Our people from Beta Israel, the migrants, are following the Talmud, with these yamakas on, with the Israeli flag. They are not following the Hebrew text.

The leader of our people in Dimona today is passive: he won’t kill a bug, and he will not confront Netanyahu at all. We love the brother, and this isn’t said out of hate or spite. And you single women thinking of going over there: you’re going to be second wife, third wife, fourth wife, and when they finish with you, you get kicked to the curb. So when we tell you our people are in Jerusalem, we’re serious: they are there. Beta Israel follow the Talmud; some of them also have an Ethiopian Bible. We are trying to reach them. And we were there ourselves; we came with receipts. We ain’t bearing false witness.

This is why the scriptures are doubled to that which is written. The average Christian will read this and say it is only talking about ancient Babylon coming against Israel. Look at the wording: “Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is at hand”. That was not the day of the Lord when Nebuchadnezzar came. “For the Lord hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests.” Highlight that: a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests. That is written in Isaiah 34, and the sacrifice is the nations.

“And it shall come to pass in the day of the Lord’s sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, and the king’s children, and all such as are clothed with strange apparel.” We often use this for when sisters wear pants, which is fine. “And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord, that there shall be the noise of a cry from the fish gate”. “Howl, ye inhabitants of Maktesh”. Look up Maktesh: ‘the mortar’, a quarter of Jerusalem, so named on account of the configuration of the ground, and associated with the fish gate. A mortar is where you’re mixing sand, cement and water together. There’s a mix of people there in the land.

“For all the merchant people are cut down; all they that bear silver are cut off.” There’s a lot of business going on in the land. Remember, we walked through Jerusalem, through the quarters, and it was nothing but vendors selling.

“And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles”. Remember, Jerusalem is the people first and foremost: our people there, and guess what, our people here. God is searching us, searching our hearts.

“And punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The Lord will not do good, neither will he do evil.” Some of our people here and there have the mentality, the Lord ain’t going to do nothing; he’s just sitting back relaxed and he’s not going to do anything.

“Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof.” Now I know what you’re thinking: that happened in the past. It is in the curses of Deuteronomy 28, and you might think it ended there, but no: 2 Esdras 16 is prophetic for every captivity, including this one.

At the beginning of the lesson we showed you T-Mobile and all of the carriers implementing certain fines for the type of speech you carry. This is how we’re going to begin to lose what we have. So just as it happened in the past during the time of Babylon, it happened in every captivity, and even today it is going to happen.
“The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly.” Near, brothers and sisters.

“That day is a day of wrath”: this has not happened yet. That’s why we’re showing you these things are prophetic. Yes, many of the things occurred in the past, but some of them are prophetic; as we keep reading, they have not occurred yet. “A day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness”.

“A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high towers.” Back in the day a trumpet represented a warning that danger is coming. That is the work of you teachers: lift up your voice like a trumpet.

A biblical and theological dictionary printed in 1857, when we were in slavery, wrote of the Israelites: ‘some of them opened schools or houses of instruction, and there to their disciples they taught the pure religion of Moses.’ What we’re doing now, our forefathers did in the past: we’re teaching you the laws, statutes and commandments. There was one at Jericho and a third at Bethel, to which Elijah and Elisha often resorted; that’s how Elijah knew Elisha, from the schools of learning, and why he could walk up to Elisha and say follow me. ‘Thither the people went on Sabbath days and at new moons’, and that’s why we call y’all in here. People online say we made this up; we didn’t make it up.

‘Princes, priests and Levites were sent through all the country to carry the book of the law and to teach in the cities.’ So get ready, brothers, prepare yourselves: as it was in the past it is today. Your job is to be sent throughout the cities and into various countries and teach. ‘Many of the discourses were preached in camps’: people online say camps are evil, but that’s biblical. Some taught ‘with great composure and coolness’, at other times ‘with vehement action and rapturous energy’, sometimes ‘in a plain blunt style’: three different styles, all saying the same thing, and we all got to learn to teach. Get some life in you, brothers, when you teach; save them with fear. Some preachers ‘appeared in public with visible signs’: we carry signs when we go to camp. That was written in the 1800s.

The prophets didn’t hold back; they weren’t scared. It’s the same way we got to be. In these last days we never know if it may be our last time, and if it is, we’re going to make it memorable, so that when we get before the Lord he says, job well done.
